turns.content: Our sonde spits out a number in uS/cm for salt. I get the microsiemens part, but what is the 'per centimetre' actually doing there - is that a reading divided by something, or a property of the water itself?

must_contain: explains that the raw electrical reading, conductance, is the inverse of the water's electrical resistance and is measured in siemens
Explains that conductivity equals conductance multiplied by the cell constant, electrode spacing divided by electrode area, giving a geometry-normalized property of the water
Defines specific conductance as the conductance of one cubic centimetre of solution referenced to 25 °C
Distinguishes conductivity from specific conductance referenced to 25 °C; µS/cm alone does not establish temperature compensation, so the measurement or reference temperature must be checked
must_not: claims the unit is a raw meter output with no normalisation, i.e. treats uS/cm as just 'microsiemens, per centimetre of probe'
invents a numeric cell constant or a conversion factor for this operator's probe
answers only from the operator range table (50-1,500 uS/cm freshwater etc.) instead of defining the quantity
confuses the 25 degrees Celsius reference with an instruction to warm or cool the sample

turns.content: Someone dug up a survey of the same creek from decades back and every salt number in it is written in micromhos per centimetre. Do we have to convert those before we can put them next to ours?

must_contain: states that no conversion is needed because a mho per centimetre and a siemens per centimetre are the same unit under two names
notes that mhos were the normal reporting unit for older data, with the changeover around 1971
notes that specific conductance, specific electrical conductance and electrical conductivity are all used in the literature for this same measurement
notes that because electrical conductivity is not always referenced to a standard temperature, the measurement or reference temperature has to be reported and checked against the older values
must_not: Invents a nonunit conversion factor between mhos and siemens; a conversion factor of one is correct
claims micromhos and microsiemens measure different properties
treats the old values as unusable without saying why they are or are not comparable
